SELECTED_INDEX: 2
CONFIDENCE: 0.46
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the characteristic pyridine-type ring pattern: a very strong ring-breathing band at 1005 cm⁻¹, companion ring mode near 1028 cm⁻¹, strong C-H out-of-plane deformation at 771 cm⁻¹ and ring C=C stretches at 1595–1614 cm⁻¹. These four bands match literature Raman lines of pyridine and substituted pyridines almost exactly.  
Candidate 2 (O=S(Cl)c1ccccn1) is the only molecule that contains a pyridine ring; other candidates are benzene, thiophene or non-aromatic rings. In addition, its sulfinyl chloride group provides an intense S=O stretch expected near 1030 cm⁻¹ (matching the 1028 cm⁻¹ peak) and an S–Cl stretch in the 600–700 cm⁻¹ region (observed peak at 620 cm⁻¹). The combination of the pyridine core plus a sulfinyl chloride substituent explains all prominent observed peaks, whereas the other candidates lack the pyridine ring and/or suitable S=O and S–Cl modes.
